# Upstream watch rows

Each `*.json` file here is one row for [`watch-upstream.yml`](../workflows/watch-upstream.yml). The workflow loads them all with [`scripts/load-upstream-watches.mjs`](../../scripts/load-upstream-watches.mjs) and, for each open tracking issue, comments when the upstream issue or pull request moves (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2673).

They are separate files so that two pull requests that each add a row never edit the same line. When every row lived in one JSON string in the workflow, any two such pull requests conflicted, and a resolution that kept one side dropped the other side's rows without anything noticing.

## Adding a row

Add one file named `<tracker>-<owner>-<repo>-<number>.json`, holding one object:

```json
{
    "tracker": 1729,
    "repo": "pestphp/pest-plugin-mutate",
    "kind": "pr",
    "number": 38,
    "composer": "pestphp/pest-plugin-mutate"
}
```

- `tracker` is the issue in this repository that the comments go on. Closing it turns its watch off.
- `repo`, `kind` (`issue` or `pr`) and `number` name the upstream thread.
- `composer` is optional. It also reports a Packagist release newer than the version in `composer.lock`. Leave it out for a package that releases every week or so, because it would notify on every release.
- `released` is optional, and only for a `pr` row: `"released": true`. Once the pull request has merged, the watch also comments once when the newest stable tag on the pull request's base-branch line contains the merge commit, so it reports the release that carries the fix rather than every release (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727). A base of `13.x` reads `v13.*` tags only; any other base reads every stable tag. Use it on a row whose follow-up waits on a release, such as dropping a local patch.

Then add a note below saying why the row earns its place and why it tracks the ticket it does. The loader rejects a file that does not parse, has an unknown key, has the wrong shape, or does not match its own name. It also fails the run when there are no row files at all, so a wrong path can never pass as "nothing to watch". When the last row is retired, disable the workflow in the Actions tab rather than leaving the directory empty.

## Retiring a row

Delete its file and its note once the signal has fired and the tracker records the outcome (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1898).

## What is watched today

A row earns its place only if a terminal signal would make us do something. Every Pest patch still in `patches/` with an open upstream report is watched here. UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1812 needed no row: upstream had already released its fix.

- **`1992-pestphp-pest-1820.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest#1820`, which resolves the git origin in linked worktrees and so changes Tia's cache key (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1924). Whichever way it lands, #1992 has to record the outcome and retire this watch. No `composer` key: `pestphp/pest` ships roughly twice a week (six stable tags between v5.0.1 and v5.1.1 in a fortnight), so a release-polling row would post about a hundred notifications a year, and the hazard it would poll for is one #1992 already removed by pinning the cache to `tests/.pest/tia`.
- **`2041-pestphp-pest-1813.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest#1813`, which replaces the Symfony Finder query in `Fingerprint::isTrackedByGit()` with `git check-ignore` and so fixes the structural fingerprint reading `null` for every tracked file in an ephemeral worktree (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1996). A merge means `composer test:tia`'s blindness guard can be retired, which is #2041's whole scope. It tracks #2041 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1996 deliberately: UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1996 closes when its own pull request merges, which would retire this row before its signal could arrive. No `composer` key, for the same reason as the row above.
- **`2419-pestphp-pest-plugin-browser-276.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest-plugin-browser#276`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1816, which gives each retry attempt the configured timeout instead of a fixed second. A merge means the `pest-plugin-browser-per-attempt-timeout` patch can be removed once a release carries it, which is #2419's scope, so the row tracks #2419 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1816. No `composer` key: v5.0.1 is already past the locked v5.0.0 and does not carry the fix, so a release-polling row would notify on its first run with nothing to do. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `5.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727).
- **`2420-pestphp-pest-plugin-browser-277.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest-plugin-browser#277`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1814, which fails a request when the Playwright connection closes instead of spinning. A merge means the `pest-plugin-browser-client-bounded-requests` patch can go once a release carries it, which is #2420's scope. No `composer` key, for the same reason as the row above. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `5.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727).
- **`2437-pestphp-pest-plugin-browser-254.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest-plugin-browser#254`, a pull request by another contributor that fixes the orphaned `playwright run-server` from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1818 by exec-prefixing the server command on POSIX. UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1818 adopted it rather than opening a competing one. A merge means the `pest-plugin-browser-server-no-shell` patch can go once a release carries it, which is #2437's scope. No `composer` key, for the same reason. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `5.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727).
- **`1931-statamic-cms-15529.json`** tracks `statamic/cms#15529`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1962 and UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2415, which stops field conditions treating booleans as empty. (Numbers were already fixed upstream in v6.30.0.) A merge is one of the upstream fixes #1931 waits on before retiring the local field-conditions evaluator, so the row tracks #1931, since UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1962 and UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2415 close now. No `composer` key: `statamic/cms` tagged twelve stable releases between 2026-08-19 and 2026-10-08, so polling would notify on nearly every run. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `6.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727). The fix is merged, and no `6.x` tag contained it on 2026-09-30, so that release is what #1931 is waiting on.
- **`1931-statamic-cms-15531.json`** tracks `statamic/cms#15531`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1963 and UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2416, which makes `contains_any` match its values literally instead of as a regular expression. - **`1931-statamic-cms-15535.json`** tracks `statamic/cms#15535`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1965 and UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2418, which stops a `contains` field condition throwing a `TypeError` when the field's value is an object. It is a fourth upstream fix #1931 waits on, so the row tracks #1931, which stays open, rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2418, which closes now. No `composer` key, for the same reason. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `6.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727). - **`1931-statamic-cms-15552.json`** is an ISSUE row. It tracks `statamic/cms#15552`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1929, which reports that `Validator.passesCondition()` evaluates standard field conditions with `eval()`, so a Content Security Policy without `'unsafe-eval'` breaks conditional fields on public forms. A close means Statamic has fixed or declined it, and #1931 decides what that means for the local evaluator UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1902 built, so the row tracks #1931. The fix pull request, `statamic/cms#15564`, has its own row below, and either may move first. No `composer` key, for the same release-cadence reason as the `1931-statamic-cms-15529.json` row.
- **`1931-statamic-cms-15564.json`** tracks `statamic/cms#15564`, opened from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1930, which replaces the `eval()` in `Validator.passesCondition()` with a table of the eight comparison operators, decoding the JSON-encoded string operands so the results match `eval()`'s. Merging it closes `statamic/cms#15552`, the issue row above. A release carrying it is one of the upstream fixes #1931 waits on before retiring the local field-conditions evaluator, so the row tracks #1931 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1930, which closes when this row is added. No `composer` key, for the same release-cadence reason as the `1931-statamic-cms-15529.json` row. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest release on the `6.x` line contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727).
- **`2676-pestphp-pest-plugin-mutate-43.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest-plugin-mutate#43`, an open pull request that rewrites the same `--filter` construction in `MutationTest::start()` as the `pest-plugin-mutate-windows-filter-length` patch (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2578), and the plugin's releases (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2677). UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2576 decided to report the five local `pest-plugin-mutate` patches (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2322, UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2327, UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2524, UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2570, UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2578) upstream together once the plugin shows activity, and either signal is that activity. UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2327 has since left that batch: its issue was already filed, so its pull request went out on its own (see the `2330` row below), and #2676 now covers the other four. A release also matters on its own: several of the patches edit `MutationTest::start()`, so a release touching it can stop them applying, and under `composer-exit-on-patch-failure: true` that fails `composer install`. It tracks #2676, the ticket that files those reports. This row carries a `composer` key, unlike the rows above, because the plugin has not released since `v5.0.2` on 2026-08-10, which is the version `composer.lock` installs, so a first run has nothing to report.
- **`2330-pestphp-pest-plugin-mutate-46.json`** tracks `pestphp/pest-plugin-mutate#46`, opened from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2329, which fixes two of the three defects reported in `pestphp/pest#1942` (filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2328): a bare `@pest-mutate-ignore` that suppresses nothing when followed by whitespace or a doc block's closing `*/`, and one that inherits an earlier line's mutator list. Those are the defects the `pest-plugin-mutate-annotation-parsing` patch fixes locally (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2327). #2330 updates `pest-plugin-mutate` and removes that patch once a release carries the fix, so the row tracks #2330 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2329, which closes when this row is added. It carries `released`, so the watch also comments once when the newest stable tag contains the merge (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2727); the base is `5.x`, so every stable tag is read. It replaces the issue row this repository used to carry for `pestphp/pest#1942`. That issue also reports a third defect, an unchecked mutation write, which #46 does not fix, so #1942 is expected to stay open after the merge and could never have signaled the release. No `composer` key: the plugin's release signal already belongs to `2676-pestphp-pest-plugin-mutate-43.json`.
- **`2724-statamic-docs-2003.json`** is an ISSUE row. It tracks `statamic/docs#2003`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1498, which asks for documentation of how a config-field Vue component reads its blueprint siblings, the undocumented `suggestableConditionFieldsProvider` inject that UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1393's `DateFieldSelectFieldtype.vue` relies on. A close means Statamic has answered, and acting on the answer is #2724's scope: move the consumer to a supported alternative if one is named, or record the outcome. It tracks #2724, not UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1498, because UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1498 closed once the request was posted (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2723). No `composer` key: `statamic/docs` is not a package this site installs.
- **`191-statamic-ideas-1490.json`** is an ISSUE row. It tracks `statamic/ideas#1490`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1396, which asks Statamic to export the Assets fieldtype's selector, browser and uploader components so a multi-container fieldtype can be built from them. #191, the multi-container fieldtype itself, is already blocked by that request and is what acts on the answer, so the row tracks #191 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1396, which closed once the request was posted (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2723). No `composer` key: `statamic/ideas` is a request tracker, not a package.
- **`486-statamic-ideas-1491.json`** is an ISSUE row. It tracks `statamic/ideas#1491`, filed from UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1397, which asks for an asset container's file-type rules to be applied in the uploader before upload. #486, restoring the upload picker's `accept` and drag-drop validation, is already blocked by that request and acts on the answer, so the row tracks #486 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1397 (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2723). No `composer` key, for the same reason.
- **`198-statamic-ideas-140.json`** is an ISSUE row. It tracks `statamic/ideas#140`, the existing request for per-row collapse on Grid fields that UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1398 added this site's case to. #198, adding collapse to the extended Grid fieldtype, is already blocked by that request and acts on the answer, so the row tracks #198 rather than UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#1398 (UAMS-Web/uams-statamic-archive#2723).
